title: Africa 8 of 8 · Indian Ocean Islands
edition: Africa countries · Eight regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Africa episode eight of eight. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.

Four island countries finish our Africa route: Madagascar, Comoros, Mauritius and Seychelles. The three smaller countries use labelled supplemental views, starting with a regional locator before each close-up.

states.name: Madagascar
lines: Madagascar is the large island east of Mozambique, separated from mainland Africa by the Mozambique Channel. The smaller Indian Ocean island countries lie around and beyond it.
The rainforests of the Atsinanana protect habitats for lemurs and many other species unique to Madagascar. Long isolation helped produce an extraordinary living world unlike the mainland’s.
Picture lemurs on the great island beside Africa. Madagascar is the large anchor; use it to locate Comoros northwest, Mauritius east and Seychelles farther north.
states.transition: Let's bring Madagascar and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Comoros
lines: Comoros lies between northern Mozambique and northern Madagascar. This labelled supplemental view shows the Union of the Comoros islands of Grande Comore, Mohéli and Anjouan.
Mount Karthala on Grande Comore is an active volcano. The islands’ volcanic origin gives us a vivid way to remember this small country in the northern Mozambique Channel.
Picture a volcano northwest of Madagascar. Nearby Mayotte is administered by France and claimed by Comoros; it is not counted as an additional country or shown as an administered Union island here.

states.name: Mauritius
lines: Mauritius lies east of Madagascar in the Indian Ocean. The main island is small, so we move from a regional locator into a labelled supplemental view.
Aapravasi Ghat in Port Louis preserves the remains of an immigration depot associated with indentured labour. Many people arrived from India to work in the island’s sugar industry.
Picture an arrival depot on a small island east of Madagascar. Mauritius is south of Seychelles; nearby Réunion is French territory and is not another country in this series.

states.name: Seychelles
lines: Seychelles is an Indian Ocean archipelago northeast of Madagascar and north of Mauritius. This close view centres on Mahé, one of its main granitic islands.
Farther southwest in the same country, Aldabra Atoll shelters giant tortoises around a shallow lagoon. Seychelles includes widely separated island groups, not only the islands near Mahé.
Picture giant tortoises across a scattered island country. Keep Seychelles north of Mauritius, and remember that the Mahé close-up does not show the distant Aldabra group.

recap: Madagascar is the large island beside Mozambique. Comoros lies northwest of its northern end, Mauritius farther east, and Seychelles farther north. Remember lemurs, a volcano, the arrival depot and giant tortoises.

Across eight episodes we have covered fifty-four countries once each, plus Western Sahara as a disputed-territory stop. Somaliland was shown within Somalia. Four missing island countries used supplemental maps with real geographic positions and relative scale.
